text:
matt: Quick question — for per-org rate limits should we standardize on RPM or prefer token-based TPM + concurrency caps? Thinking about spikes from embeddings jobs.

jess: We currently have token-based billing but rate enforcement is per-request RPM. That mismatch causes weird edgecases.

nate: +1 to hybrid. RPM for long-term fair share, concurrency cap for burst control. Keep TPM for billing only.

priya: Concurrency needs to be cheap to evaluate at the router. We should avoid per-req token counting in the hot path.

thom: If we do RPM + concurrency, what do we do about polyphonic clients that open 100 short requests? RPM can't stop connection storm.

matt: Proposal: per-org sliding window RPM (1m) + soft concurrency cap with short backoff. Hard cap only for orgs that abuse. Policy config example:

```json
{
  "rpm": 6000,
  "concurrency": 50,
  "burst_window_secs": 10,
  "burst_capacity": 150
}
```

jess: That burst_window/burst_capacity is interesting. How do we surface this in console? Need to show real-time token burn and queued requests.

priya: Telemetry: emit per-org concurrent_requests gauge, rpm_ewma, last_burst_start. That way ops/console can graph immediately.

nate: Also we need transport-level enforcement: token bucket per org at edge + concurrency semaphore at runtime. Token counting for TPM stays async.

thom: Rollout plan: feature flag per org + metrics to detect false positives. Start with a canary org subset.

matt: UX: Console should let org admins set preferred policy from presets (Balanced / Low-latency / Cost-optimized) which map to RPM/TPM/concurrency tunings.

jess: +1. Need warnings when switching policies (eg. reducing concurrency for active apps).

quota-bot: deploy note: new router patch will add concurrency enforcement v1 — no tenant defaults changed.

matt: Action items: Priya to draft telemetry schema, Nate to prototype edge token bucket + semaphore, Jess to design console presets. Thom to write rollout playbook. I'll open PRs.

jess: Thanks — can we sync tomorrow 11am? Quick sync ok.

nate: I'll be there. Adding rough timeline to thread.
